chapter: Second European tour and the crash
title: Arthur Lyons leaves for Hollywood; Spadoni sends him back to Europe
summary: Lyons hands his business to his brother and goes to Hollywood, and Wooding returns to Europe under Spadoni through Eddie Duisberg.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, in other words, when you came back in 1927, from South America, you hooked up again with Arthur Lyons.
Whom you had dissassociated yourself from in Europe, right?
And did he -- he was then responsible for your going back to Europe?

For the vaudeville there. And then he turned his business over to -- in '27 or the early part of '28, over to his brother Sam Lyons. And he went to, went out to Hollywood, because everything was moving out that way. And Arthur was really up on the ball. I think he ended up by being the manager for Jack Benny and some big acts out there. Because he was a go-getter. I mean, he -- when I moved him out of that office by him putting us in the Club Alabam, he never looked back. He was somebody that, I wish that I could have had an Arthur Lyons after that.

But, in going back to Europe -- I went back for Paul Spadoni, and the man, the errand boy that he sent -- a fellow named Eddie Dussberg -- to meet us in Hamburg, this fellow turned out by using my band as a battle ram. He turned out to have the biggest theater, the Winter Garden theater, in Berlin. Of the vaudeville houses, see. And he turned out to be a great man until Hitler come along and run us both out of there.
